newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU ministers to vet Spanish, Portugese EMU plans.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers to vet Spanish, Portugese EMU plans.

text.p: European Union finance ministers on Monday are expected to shower praise on recent efforts by Spain and Portugal to meet the preconditions of a single currency.

In an examination of their so-called convergence programmes, EU diplomats said the two southern European countries should receive high marks for presenting rigorous and realistic plans to rein in public expenditure.
Both countries have submitted updated convergence plans which stretch until the year 2000.
The European Commission and the EU's Monetary Committee have already endorsed the programmes and it is widely anticipated that EU finance ministers will reach the same conclusion.
For Portugal, EU diplomats said the revised plan seemed "well balanced" and appropriate for the Portuguese economy.
Portugal is widely seen by analysts as having a good chance at qualifying for the single currency in 1999.

Spain's programme, meanwhile, was viewed as having the political backing not only of the government, but also of an overwhelming majority in Parliament and the support of regional authorities, diplomats said.
In addition, the Spanish plan was seen complying with both the Maastricht treaty's requirements and those of the Stability and Growth Pact.
